boards.title: Claimed by 9am: 10 Study Spots Worth Showing Up Early For
boards.description: Ten documented study environments across UNCW Library’s Discovery Hall and Randall Hall, with access details noted where the library specifies them.

cards.title: Grand Reading Room
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Use the semi-private carrels for individual work, and keep conversations elsewhere: the room is designated for quiet study only.
cards.short_summary: A silent-study room with ample seating and 12 semi-private carrels.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies DH3001 as a non-reservable, quiet-study-only Grand Reading Room with a 105-person maximum capacity; its expansion page notes 12 semi-private study carrels.
cards.source_title: Space Usage and Reservation Guidelines | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: Not reservable. Quiet study only; covered drinks are allowed but food is not.

cards.title: The Lookout
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Settle in by the campus-facing windows for reading or planning; bring only a covered drink, since food is not allowed.
cards.short_summary: A third-floor library space with expansive campus views and a mural.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes The Lookout as a third-floor space with expansive windows overlooking campus, and library guidelines list it as DH3013, non-reservable, with a capacity of 30.
cards.access_notes: Not reservable; maximum capacity 30. Covered drinks only and no food.

cards.title: The Living Room
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall, UNCW Library
cards.notes: Bring a collaborative task and use the shared seating; this is an open space, so keep adjacent quiet-study areas in mind.
cards.short_summary: A shared Randall Hall setting designated for collaboration and study.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW’s library expansion page identifies The Living Room as a gathering space for collaboration and study; library guidelines state it is first-come, first-served.
cards.access_notes: Open, first-come, first-served shared space. Food and drink are permitted; expected group-activity noise should remain respectful.

cards.title: Sensory Friendly Study Space
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall 2017
cards.notes: Adjust the desk, lamp, or seating to suit your focus needs, then return the setup when leaving and use headphones for audio.
cards.short_summary: A customizable individual-study room with sensory-support tools.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists RL2017 as a non-reservable sensory-friendly space for eligible OneCard holders, with adjustable desks, dimmable lamps, seating options, and noise-reduction headsets.
cards.source_title: Sensory Friendly Study Space | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: Available to UNCW students, faculty, and staff with a valid OneCard; intended for individual study. Not reservable.

cards.title: Graduate Student Study Space
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall 2048
cards.notes: Graduate students can use this card-access space for focused work; check the reservation system separately if a graduate study room is needed.
cards.short_summary: A graduate-only study area with seating, technology, and adjoining study rooms.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies RL2048 as an expanded Graduate Student Study Space and states that it is non-reservable, accessible to graduate students by OneCard tap, and has a capacity of 45.
cards.source_title: Space Usage and Reservation Guidelines | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: Accessible only to graduate students through OneCard tap. The main space is not reservable.

cards.title: Retreat at Randall
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall 2016
cards.notes: Use this named Randall Hall retreat for individual study, and follow the room’s food restriction so the environment remains suitable for everyone.
cards.short_summary: A card-access study space included in UNCW Library’s documented space inventory.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW Library’s space guidelines list Retreat at Randall (RL2016) among its named spaces, and the library privacy policy identifies it as a space requiring OneCard access.
cards.source_title: Space Usage and Reservation Guidelines | UNCW Library
cards.access_notes: OneCard access is required. Library general guidance specifically identifies Retreat at Randall as a space where food is not allowed.

cards.entity_name: Center for Southeast North Carolina Archives and History Research Room
cards.title: Archives Research Room
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, second floor
cards.notes: Plan an archive-based research session around the room’s adjacent books, manuscript collections, maps, photographs, and audiovisual materials.
cards.short_summary: A research room beside UNCW archival and special-collections materials.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW states that Discovery Hall’s second floor includes the Center for Southeast North Carolina Archives and History and a unified research room adjacent to its books and manuscript collections.
cards.access_notes: Consult the library before a visit for current research-room procedures and collection access.

cards.title: Visualization and Analysis Lab
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall 1072
cards.notes: Use this lab when a project needs large-scale visual work; contact library facilities first about collaboration, class, event, or presentation use.
cards.short_summary: A data-visualization lab centered on a 30-foot display wall.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW describes DH1072 as a Visualization and Analysis Lab with an immersive 30-foot video display wall, a high-performance computer, and use for visualization-related classes, events, presentations, and collaboration.
cards.access_notes: For classes, events, presentations, or visualization collaboration; UNCW directs users to contact rlfacility@uncw.edu for details.

cards.title: Study Room RL1001C4
cards.subtitle: Randall Hall, first floor
cards.notes: Reserve this six-seat room for a small group or use it when unreserved; take advantage of the whiteboard, power, and movable tables.
cards.short_summary: A six-seat, accessible study room with natural light and a whiteboard.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW lists RL1001C4 as a first-floor Randall Hall study room for six with natural light, movable tables and chairs, power, and a wall-mounted whiteboard.
cards.access_notes: Current UNCW students, staff, and faculty may reserve it. When unreserved, it is first-come, first-served.

cards.entity_name: Discovery Hall Third-Floor Open Study Areas
cards.title: Discovery Hall Third-Floor Open Study Areas
cards.subtitle: Discovery Hall, third floor
cards.notes: Choose an open seat for independent work and keep your volume low: Discovery Hall’s third floor is designated as a quiet space.
cards.short_summary: Open third-floor study seating with nearby computing and printing.
cards.evidence_claim: UNCW identifies Discovery Hall’s third floor as containing open study areas, open computing, and iPrint stations; its noise policy designates the floor as a quiet space.
cards.access_notes: Open study area, not a reservable room. Keep noise to a minimum and keep phones on silent, per the library noise policy.
